why: The key was parsed by both libraries, emitted by the control plane when non-empty, and applied by no renderer: a layout declaring it produced an unpartitioned table and said nothing. Nothing populates it today so no issued map has ever carried one, but a hand-written map legally may - the no-account mode is a documented mode - and a storage decision silently dropped out of a signed document is the worst of the three available answers. Rendering it would mean designing two dialect-specific features with no requirement behind them and interpolating a caller's SQL fragment into DDL, so it fails closed instead. Found by a third implementation while writing §7a, which is the same class as `provisional`, `basis`, `in_use` and `key_id` before it: a field whose value reaches nobody. Accepting it again the day partitioning exists is a loosening and therefore a bump, which is the right price for the key starting to mean something. That day came on 23 September 2026: partitioning is placement map contract 5, and this document declares contract 1, so the refusal stands for it and for every document declaring less than 5. The bump is what lets the same key be refused here and rendered there without either library guessing.
